original_question: For integers m >= 1, let C_{m,n} be defined by sum_{n>=0} C_{m,n} q^n = 1/(q^m; q^{2m})_infty, where (a; q)_infty := product_{j>=0} (1-a q^j). The paper proves that for integers m, k >= 1, one has C_{m,n} congruent to 0 modulo m whenever n is congruent to one of 0, 1, ..., k-1 modulo k. Can one prove congruences for the family C_{m,n} for all moduli, and not only for the moduli covered by those residue-class congruences?
